Definition
[proper action; orbit; isotropy group]

Source: petersen:page-0221

An action of a topological group $H$ on $M$ is proper if $H\times M\to M\times M$, $(h,p)\mapsto (hp,p)$, is proper. The orbit through $p$ is $Hp=\{ hp\mid h\in H\} $; $H\backslash M$ carries the quotient topology, making $M\to H\backslash M$ continuous and open, second countable, and Hausdorff when the action is proper. The isotropy group at $p$ is $H_p=\{ h\in H\mid hp=p\} $; along an orbit $H_{hp}=hH_ph^{-1}$, $H_p$ is compact for proper actions, and $H/H_p\to Hp$ is a homeomorphism. $H$ acts freely if $H_p=\{ e\} $ for all $p$.
